name: Ahiezer
title: Prince of the tribe of Dan
lifespan: Unknown; Exodus period (circa 1400s or 1200s BC, depending on chronological model)
summary: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, served as tribal prince and military commander for the tribe of Dan during the wilderness journey after leaving Egypt. He was chosen by God to stand beside Moses as leader of his tribe when the Israelites were mustered in the Sinai desert. With its 62,700 fighting men, Dan formed one of the largest tribes. In the camp arrangement around the tabernacle, Ahiezer's division was positioned on the north side, together with the tribes of Asher and Naphtali. During the march, Dan held the strategically vital position as the rear guard for all Israel's camp. At the dedication of the altar, Ahiezer presented his offering on the tenth day, consisting of a silver plate, a silver basin, a gold bowl with incense, along with sacrificial animals for burnt offerings, sin offerings, and peace offerings—the same gift that each of the other tribal princes brought.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as tribal leader of Dan
keyEvents.description: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, was appointed by God as the tribal leader and representative of the tribe of Dan to assist Moses with the census in the wilderness of Sinai.

keyEvents.title: The Census in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: During the census in the wilderness of Sinai, Ahiezer led the counting of the tribe of Dan, which numbered 62,700 men fit for military service.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement Around the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Ahiezer was appointed to lead the camp of Dan, which was positioned on the north side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Asher and Naphtali.

keyEvents.title: Rear Guard During the March
keyEvents.description: Ahiezer led the division under the banner of Dan as the last group to break camp during the march through the wilderness, thus serving as the rear guard for the entire Israelite camp.

keyEvents.title: Offering at the Dedication of the Altar
keyEvents.description: On the tenth day of the altar's dedication, Ahiezer brought his offering, which included a silver plate, a silver basin, a gold bowl with incense, an ox, a ram, a lamb, and a male goat for burnt offerings, sin offerings, and peace offerings.

keyEvents.title: Commander Over Dan's Forces
keyEvents.description: Ahiezer was appointed as commander over the entire military force of the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

versions.summary: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, was the chosen leader of the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings. He was appointed by God to assist Moses in the census and served as chief over his tribe. He also brought offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle.

versions.reason: [minor] The title 'Leader of the Tribe of Dan' is correct but could be made more descriptive by including the role of chief/tribal prince, which is the typical designation in Numbers.; [major] The roles are incomplete. Ahiezer was not merely a 'leader,' but also served as tribal prince/chief and military commander. These roles should be added to provide a more complete picture.; [minor] The summary is good but could mention that he brought offerings on the tenth day, placing him in the sequence of tribal princes. The wording could be improved slightly.; [minor] 'c. 1500 BC' is a reasonable approximation for the Exodus period, but the dating of the Exodus is debated (c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC depending on chronology). A broader formulation such as 'Unknown; Exodus period' or 'c. 14th century BC' could be more accurate for the early dating.; [minor] The description states 'the tenth day after the dedication of the altar,' but the text in Numbers 7 describes that Ahiezer brought his offering on the tenth day of the dedication, not ten days after the dedication.; [major] Footnotes are missing. Notes should be added regarding the meaning of the name, the historical context for the role of tribal princes, and about the camp arrangement.

versions.summary: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, was the tribal leader of the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' wilderness journey. He was appointed by God to assist Moses in the census in the Sinai desert and served as chief and military commander over his tribe. Dan numbered 62,700 men fit for battle. Ahiezer led Dan's camp on the north side of the tabernacle, together with the tribes of Asher and Naphtali, and during the march his division served as the rear guard. On the tenth day of the altar dedication he brought his offering, consisting of a silver plate, a silver bowl, a gold bowl for incense, as well as animals for various sacrifices.
versions.title: Prince of the tribe of Dan
versions.reason: [minor] The summary is good, but on the tenth day it should be clarified that the offering also included a bull, a ram, and a lamb—not just "animals for various offerings." However, the wording is acceptable as a concise summary. No change needed.; [minor] The tenth day of the altar dedication is correct according to Num 7:66. The order among the tribal leaders is accurate—Ahiezer was number ten.; [minor] The name Ahiezer more likely means "my brother is help" or "brother for help." Some scholars interpret it as "my (divine) brother is a helper." It may be noted that "ach" (brother) in theophoric names sometimes refers to a divine figure, not necessarily a literal brother. A small clarification has been added in the revised version.; [minor] The dating "around the 1400s BC" depends on the chronological model. An early date places the exodus around 1446 BC, while a late date places it around 1260 BC. A more neutral formulation could be "around the 1400s or 1200s BC."

footnotes.text: The name Ahiezer (Hebrew: אֲחִיעֶזֶר, 'Achi'ezer') can be translated as 'my brother is help' or 'brother for help'. In theophoric Semitic names, 'ach' (brother) may refer to a divine figure rather than a biological relative, so the name possibly expresses 'the divine brother is (my) helper'.

Ammishaddai (Hebrew: עַמִּישַׁדָּי), Ahiezer's father, has a name meaning 'my people are El Shaddai' or 'Shaddai is my kinsman'. This is a theophoric name linked to the divine name El Shaddai, which was central in the patriarchal period and continued into the Exodus era.

The camp arrangement in Numbers 2 placed Dan, Asher, and Naphtali on the north side of the tabernacle. This military and cultic organization of a central sanctuary surrounded by tribal groups in four cardinal directions has parallels in known Egyptian and Mesopotamian camp structures from the second millennium BCE, which has been discussed in research on wilderness journey narratives.

Ahiezer's offering on the tenth day (Num 7:66–71) was identical to those of the other tribal leaders. This uniformity emphasizes the equality among the tribes in the cultic order, even though the sequence itself may reflect a specific ranking or geographical placement around the tabernacle.

The tribe of Dan, which Ahiezer led, were descendants of Dan, son of Jacob and his maidservant Bilhah (Gen 30:5–6). The tribe was assigned the rear-guard position during the march (Num 10:25), a militarily important role that involved protecting the camp from enemy attacks coming from behind.

The census in Numbers 1 recorded 62,700 fighting men in the tribe of Dan, making it one of the largest tribes. The Hebrew word 'elef' (אֶלֶף), translated as 'thousand', has been subject to academic debate—some scholars suggest it may refer to military units or clans rather than the literal number thousand.
